## Exchange message matching and in-process copies (`SyncOptions.phyid`) {#sec-ch14-msgmatch}

Local symbols (flagged to the editor): $\phi$ the `phyid` of a sync; $\ell$ a local block index (@eq-ch14-launch-rank);
$\beta$ a buffer id; $n$ the index of a variable in an exchange; $T$ a message tag; $b$ the blocks per process.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: how the buffers of one ghost sync (@sec-ch03-exchange) reach their neighbours. A remote neighbour gets one
tagged message per variable; a neighbour in the same process gets a direct copy after all local blocks have
arrived. **Switch**: `SyncOptions.phyid` ($0 \le \phi < 64$). **Default**: $\phi = 0$. **Requires**: a process
group for remote neighbours. **Order**: exact copy. **Defining equation**: @eq-ch14-msgmatch-tag.
:::

A sync is serialise, launch, finalise. `launch_exchange` first does the in-process copies and then posts the remote
messages. The remote message of variable $n$ from a block to the buffer $\beta$ of local block $\ell$ in another
process has the tag of @eq-ch14-msgmatch-tag. Same-process neighbours never use the process group: their buffers are
copied in memory once all $b$ blocks of the process have reached the same sync.

### Derivation

The tag must identify the receiving block, the buffer and the variable, so that two messages between the same pair
of processes never match each other's receive. With at most 32 buffer ids, 32 local blocks per $\phi$ and 64 values of
$\phi$, the base tag fills 16 bits:

$$
T_0 = 1024\,\phi + 32\,\ell + \beta, \qquad 0 \le T_0 < 65536, \qquad T = T_0 + 65536\,n .
$$ {#eq-ch14-msgmatch-tag}

Since $T_0 < 65536$, the map $(T_0, n) \mapsto T$ is one to one: $n = \lfloor T / 65536 \rfloor$ and
$T_0 = T \bmod 65536$. $T_0$ itself is one to one in $(\phi, \ell, \beta)$ as long as $\beta < 32$ and $32\ell + \beta
< 1024$, that is $\ell < 32$ (27 buffer ids is the largest, on `cubed`). `make_comm_tag` enforces $0 \le T_0 < 65536$,
which rejects $\phi \ge 64$ or $\phi < 0$ ([`layout.hpp:161-170`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/layout.hpp#L161-L170)).
`exchange_each_var` refuses more than 32768 variables, which keeps $T$ below $2^{31}$
([`layout.cpp:652-666`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/layout.cpp#L652-L666)). The per-block bound $\ell < 32$ is not checked
separately. The send tag uses the receiver's $\ell$ and the receiver's buffer id, so the sender computes what the
receiver posts.

Two other kinds of message share the process group:

1. Block-to-block messages (`send_to_block`, `recv_from_block`), used by the $x_1$ relays of @sec-ch03-x1seams.
   They add $65536\,(\ell_\text{send}\, b + \ell_\text{recv})$ to a caller tag. With $b \le 16$ (checked) the factor is
   below 256, so the low 16 bits stay the caller's tag (`send_to_block`, [`layout.cpp:849-877`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/layout.cpp#L849-L877)).
   The comment above `send_to_block` [`layout.hpp:272-280`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/layout.hpp#L272-L280) gives the argument: the hydro relay
   tags (`0x77xx`) are not values of $T_0$ at $b \le 16$, and the total stays below the gather tags.
2. `gather_x1` uses $2^{24} + \ell_\text{send}\, b + \ell_\text{recv}$
   ([`layout.cpp:777-847`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/layout.cpp#L777-L847)).

### Numerical method

**Remote neighbours.** `exchange_remote` walks the neighbour offsets and skips physical faces and absent neighbours.
A neighbour that is the block itself (a periodic direction with one block) is copied from the send buffer to the
opposite receive buffer. A neighbour in another process becomes one operation with the send and receive tags
of @eq-ch14-msgmatch-tag. All operations of the block are then posted under one process-wide mutex. On UCX they are
posted inside one coalescing group (`exchange_remote`, [`layout.cpp:548-650`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/layout.cpp#L548-L650)). With two blocks in a
periodic direction, the first block walks that direction in reverse order (`dx_sgn = -1`; the code comment says
"swap the order of first block for periodic condition"). The set of offsets is unchanged, only the posting order.
The comment gives no reason; one hypothesis, not tested, is that it keeps the two messages to the same neighbour in
the order that neighbour posts them. The cubed-sphere layout posts its
remote operations under its own mutex and without a coalescing group
(`g_cubed_sphere_comm_mutex`, [`cubed_sphere_layout.cpp:1036-1048`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp#L1036-L1048)).

**Same-process neighbours.** `_prepare_local_exchange` is a rendezvous keyed by the sync signature: process, $b$,
`dim`, $\phi$, type and the phase and corner flags (`_prepare_local_exchange`, [`layout.cpp:279-387`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/layout.cpp#L279-L387)).
Each block increments an arrival count. The last block to arrive copies every same-process buffer pair
(`_copy_local_exchange_buffers`, [`layout.cpp:419-475`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/layout.cpp#L419-L475)) and releases the others.
A generation counter keeps one sync's release from waking a block that has already entered the next. An exception
in the copy is re-thrown in every block of the process. On a CUDA device each block records an arrival event on its
stream; the copying block waits on all of them and records a completion event that the others wait on
(@sec-ch14-bpp). This rendezvous has no timeout.

**In-process boards.** Messages between blocks of one process that are not a whole sync go through boards guarded by
the same mutex: the $x_1$ reference anchors (`take_x1_anchor`), per-tag mailboxes (`post_to_local_block`,
`take_from_local_block`) and the column board of `gather_x1`. The anchor and mailbox waits time out after
5 minutes with an error that names the cause: local blocks must run concurrently, or from the top of the $x_1$
column down (`take_x1_anchor`, [`layout.cpp:879-970`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/layout.cpp#L879-L970)).

**Buffers.** Send and receive buffers are kept per block and reused when the same sync runs again; `test_exchange`
checks that their data pointers do not change.

pointer and neighbour checks are in `main` of [`test_exchange.cpp:218-319`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_exchange.cpp#L218-L319).
Their pass status at the pin was not run for this chapter. No test posts two variables between the same two
processes with tags that would alias if the offset were missing; the argument above is the evidence.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- A caller that steps the local blocks one after another instead of concurrently waits 5 minutes at the first
  board and then stops; at the sync rendezvous it waits forever. `Mesh` always runs them concurrently
  (@sec-ch14-bpp).
- The bound $\ell < 32$ on local blocks for the base tag is implied, not checked; block-to-block messages check
  $b \le 16$.
:::
